subject.title: fix: prevent operational notices from leaking to source chats

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this permanent global operational-notice contract, including fail-closed source suppression when a configured operator-session redirect cannot be written?
rationale: The implementation is technically coherent, but choosing privacy over notice availability on redirect failure—and exposing that choice through config, durable session state, and plugin API—is a product and security-boundary decision that code inspection cannot authorize.

options.title: Approve the current privacy-first contract
options.body: Accept always/once/redirect/silent as permanent modes and keep redirect failures source-silent with operator-visible logging and documentation.

options.title: Require durable redirect recovery
options.body: Delay redirect mode until failed operator-session writes can be retained for operator-only retry without exposing the notice to the source chat.

options.title: Narrow this PR to non-redirect modes
options.body: Land always, once, and silent while deferring redirect and its privacy-versus-availability contract to separate owner-approved work.

recommendation.title: Approve the current privacy-first contract
recommendation.body: Accept always/once/redirect/silent as permanent modes and keep redirect failures source-silent with operator-visible logging and documentation.

likelyOwner.reason: His current-main history owns the visible-reply, suppression, session, heartbeat, and plugin surfaces needed to approve this cross-boundary contract.
